name: Electrowetting brain shunt
subtitle: a hydrocephalus drain opened and closed by voltage

effects.effect: a voltage makes a liquid spread over a surface instead of beading up

effect: a voltage makes a liquid spread over a surface instead of beading up
how: Children with fluid building up in the brain (hydrocephalus) rely on a drain tube whose spring valve often clogs or drains wrongly, and about half need another operation within two years. This drain's valve has no moving parts: a plug with water-repelling pores stays shut until a small voltage lets the fluid wet them and flow through (electrocapillarity), so a pressure sensor and chip open it exactly when needed.
obstacle: Proteins in brain fluid coat the pores over months and change how easily they wet.
why: Shunt failure means repeated brain surgery for children; a valve with no moving parts could end that.
real: Active CSF shunts use electroactive polymers, electromechanical or electrokinetic actuators, and capillary-electrowetting valves exist separately, but no electrowetting hydrocephalus shunt valve was found.
